result.title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can answer many factual questions correctly, but a correct answer is not necessarily a supported one. For an LLM agent, a knowledge graph (KG) plays two roles: as a source of answers, it supplies facts that the model lacks; as a source of evidence, it supplies the supporting triples that make an answer traceable and auditable. However, existing KG agents treat the KG only as a source of answers: their training data carries answers but not evidence, and their training rewards check the answer but not the retrieved evidence, so agents often answer correctly without retrieving the supporting triples. We propose FoG, a framework that trains KG agents to retrieve the evidence behind their answers. FoG consists of evidence-grounded synthesis, a KG interaction agent, and an evidence-coverage process reward (ECPR): the synthesis recursively hides explicit entities behind verifiable sub-questions, so that every question carries its supporting triples by construction; the agent records the triples returned by the KG; and ECPR credits each supporting triple to the turn that first retrieves it. Experiments on three KGQA benchmarks demonstrate that FoG enables 3B--4B open-source agents to outperform substantially larger baselines in answer accuracy and evidence coverage, with zero-shot cross-KG transfer.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FoG 框架，用证据锚定的合成数据、KG 交互 agent 和证据覆盖过程奖励（ECPR），训练 KG agent 在作答时检索支撑三元组，并在三个 KGQA 基准上评估答案准确率与证据覆盖。
AI.relevance_reason: 把每条支撑三元组的奖励记到首次检索它的轮次这一 ECPR 做法，可供核查多轮视觉证据筛选与「LOOK」轮次的贡献分配和停止决策；但原文为纯文本 KGQA，迁移到视觉状态需较多改造。
